pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we enjoy reading stories and poems?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify characters and events in a text for comprehension
2. answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension
3. create mental images from the events in poems and stories

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify characters and events in a text for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify characters and events in a text for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify characters and events in a text for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify characters and events in a text for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Create mental images from the events in poems and stories

What this means
In this part you learn to create mental images from the events in poems and stories. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create mental images from the events in poems and stories.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create mental images from the events in poems and stories. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify characters and events in a text for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner. (skill: answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: create mental images from the events in poems and stories)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify characters and events in a text for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: create mental images from the events in poems and stories.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we enjoy reading stories and poems?
2. Which stories and poems have you read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify characters and events in a text for comprehension.
5. Be able to: answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
